header.question:
A document in the library contains this sentence:

> Another important tool is mechanistic analysis, i.e. studying the model’s weights and activations for understanding how it functions (Nanda et al., 2023; Olah et al., 2020).

Check what the sentence says about the work it cites against that work in the library. Does the cited source support it? Cite the page(s) of the cited source that show what it actually says.

args.query: mechanistic analysis weights activations understanding how it functions
Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
Nanda mechanistic interpretability progress measures grokking

args.quote: C. Olah, N. Cammarata, L. Schubert, G. Goh, M. Petrov, and S. Carter. Zoom in: An introduction to circuits. Distill, 5(3), Mar. 2020.

args.text:
Verdict: not supported

The sentence is on arxiv:2305.15324/v2/p12, in *Model evaluation for extreme risks*: "Another important tool is mechanistic analysis, i.e. studying the model’s weights and activations for understanding how it functions (Nanda et al., 2023; Olah et al., 2020)." It is the same sentence you quoted.

The two works it cites are not in the library as full documents. The library only shows them as bibliography entries in the same paper:

- Nanda et al., 2023 is listed on arxiv:2305.15324/v2/p17 as "N. Nanda, L. Chan, T. Lieberum, J. Smith, and J. Steinhardt. Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability. Jan. 2023."
- Olah et al., 2020 is listed on arxiv:2305.15324/v2/p18 as "C. Olah, N. Cammarata, L. Schubert, G. Goh, M. Petrov, and S. Carter. Zoom in: An introduction to circuits. Distill, 5(3), Mar. 2020."

Searches for the text of either work returned nothing, so I could not read what they say about mechanistic analysis. Their titles are about mechanistic interpretability, which is consistent with the sentence, but a title does not show that either work describes mechanistic analysis as studying a model's weights and activations to understand how it functions. The library therefore does not support the attribution. Checking it would need the full text of both works.
